title: Import seeds
description: What an import is pointed at: the items to fetch and the queries that find more of them. Like an import map it is not a record — no provenance envelope, no kind of node — and the browser never reads it; unlike an import map it says nothing about what the result means, only where to look. It is contributor-editable through the ordinary pull-request path, which is the point: which corner of Wikidata this atlas draws from is an editorial decision and belongs in a file somebody can argue with, not in the tool. tools/validate.mjs checks it; whether an item or a query exists at all is checked at import time, against the source.

kind.description: What kind of file this is. data/imports/ holds more than one, and tools/lib/read.mjs dispatches on this rather than on the file name.

source.description: The id of the source record the import cites, so a seeds file cannot be pointed at the wrong catalogue by accident.

items.description: Items named one by one, in the source's own identifier — for Wikidata, Q followed by digits. The list is what --import walks.

queries.description: Searches that find items nobody has listed by hand. Run by --candidates, which writes a list for a person to tick and nothing under data/: a query is a way of proposing records, never of creating them.

name.description: A slug naming the query, unique in the file: it is what the candidate list is grouped by.

sparql.description: The query itself, exactly as it is sent. Written by a person and readable in the diff, so what the atlas asked for is reviewable.

note.description: Why this query is here, for whoever reads the file next.

reconcile.description: Whether --reconcile may match this atlas's existing hand-written records against the source. Off by default: matching writes identifiers onto records somebody wrote.
